messages:
Alex R: quick note — i'm experimenting with splitting policy eval into a "late-bind" runtime check + precomputation. thinking about cost/latency tradeoffs. thoughts?
Maya S: what do you mean by "late-bind" exactly? how's it different from probe-led weighting?
Dmitri K: late-bind = do coarse routing at compile time, then at runtime run a lightweight scorer that checks fresh capacity/penalty windows. less cold-start for decision state.
Lena P: main worry: cache invalidation and determinism for canaries. if runtime scorer and compile scorer disagree, rollouts could flip unpredictably.
Sanjay V: also ops concern: sidecar vs in-process library have different failure/latency modes. need a simple adapter contract.
Alex R: agreed. proposal: keep the policy graph compile-time, but allow per-request "tie-breaker" scorer that only sees recent telemetry and region probes; if it errors or times out we fallback to compile route. pseudo-config:
```
policy {
  compile: graph_v3
  runtimeScorer: {
    enabled: true
    timeoutMs: 6
    features: [region_probe, recent_latency_q95, tenant_budget]
  }
  fallback: compile
}
```
Maya S: timeout 6ms seems tight. how do we ensure we don't exceed latency SLOs? we need hedging or circuit-breaker. :thinking: 
Dmitri K: hedging is doable: primary = runtime scorer, fallback = compile route, but keep an async canary path to validate decisions. note hedging multiplies request cost.
Lena P: ops needs observability: sample every N decisions and surface "runtimeScorer delta" in console (latency/cost/route difference). we also need a heatmap of how often runtime changes route vs compile.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: policy-sandbox-v2 canary -> 2026-04-02T15:00:00Z (planned)
Sanjay V: perf: runtime scorer must be O(1) mem and no KV locks. propose pre-warmed atomic ring buffer for recent telemetry, and avoid GC pressure.
Alex R: follow-ups: 1) write RFC for runtime scorer proto/interface, 2) perf microbench for 6ms scorer window, 3) canary experiment: runtimeScorer=false for 95% tenants, true for 5% then gradually ramp.
Maya S: +1 to RFC. also need compatibility semantics: runtime scorer cannot introduce routes absent from compile graph (reject or sandbox).
Dmitri K: compatibility rule: runtime scorer can only prefer routes present in compile graph. any "new route" candidate goes to "suggestions" stream for offline vetting.
Lena P: additional safety: if runtime scorer throws or exceeds timeout, increment a short-lived penalty for that tenant to avoid flip-flopping; also auto-disable runtimeScorer after N consecutive errors.
Alex R: i'll spin up the RFC draft and include a small sim harness for oscillation tests. cc @Maya S @Dmitri K for review. :rocket:
Maya S: thanks — i'll add a telemetry panel proposal in the RFC too.
Dmitri K: i'll prep the perf harness and the ring-buffer prototype.
Lena P: i'll draft the ops runbook for canary cutover and rollback steps.
Sanjay V: sounds good. keep the runtime scorer surface tiny: feature vectors only, no joins.
Alex R: cool — i'll post the RFC link here when ready.
